You are working in the Ligra graph-processing framework at /workspace.
The framework (/workspace/ligra/*.h) is COMPLETE and already implements
vertexSubset, edgeMap/edgeMapData/edgeMapDense/edgeMapDenseForward/edgeMapSparse/
edgeMapSparse_no_filter, edgeMapFilter, packEdges, vertexMap, vertexFilter,
vertexFilter2 and parallel_main. DO NOT MODIFY ANY FILE under /workspace/ligra/,
and DO NOT MODIFY /workspace/apps/Makefile or any other app's .C file.
Your ONLY writable file is the single .C file named in your task.

Build & run (apps/ has symlinks to ../ligra/*.h already):
  cd /workspace/apps && make <AppName>
Compiler line: g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o <App> <App>.C

CRITICAL framework facts (verify by reading the headers before coding):
* In the default build, parallel.h maps parallel_for -> plain `for` (single
  threaded). Code must still be written with correct atomics (CAS/writeMin/
  writeAdd) as upstream Ligra does, but execution is deterministic.
* Types: uintE/intE (32-bit by default), uintT/intT, UINT_E_MAX, INT_E_MAX.
* ligra/utils.h provides: CAS, writeMin, writeAdd, hashInt, newA, granular_for,
  sequence::plusReduce, sequence::plusScan, pbbs::* . There is NO writeOr --
  if you need atomic bitwise-or, define it locally in your .C file.
* edgeMap signature:
    edgeMap(graph<vertex>& GA, VS& vs, F f, intT threshold = -1, const flags& fl = 0)
  flags available: no_output, pack_edges, sparse_no_filter, dense_forward,
  dense_parallel, remove_duplicates, no_dense, edge_parallel.
  threshold -1 means "use GA.m/20".
* The user struct F passed to edgeMap must provide update(s,d),
  updateAtomic(s,d) and cond(d). For WEIGHTED apps the signatures are
  update(s,d,weight) / updateAtomic(s,d,weight).
* vertexMap(VS& V, F f) calls f(v) for a plain vertexSubset.
* vertexFilter(vertexSubset V, F filter) -> dense-based result.
  vertexFilter2(...) -> sparse-based result.
* vertexSubset constructors: vertexSubset(n) empty; vertexSubset(n, v) single
  vertex; vertexSubset(n, m, uintE* sparseArray); vertexSubset(n, m, bool* dense).
  Methods: isEmpty(), numNonzeros(), numRows(), toSparse(), toDense(), del(),
  vtx(i), isIn(v), dense().
* cond_true(d) is provided for "always true" cond functions.
* Every app is a template function:
    template <class vertex> void Compute(graph<vertex>& GA, commandLine P) {...}
  It MUST be a template over vertex, because parallel_main instantiates it for
  symmetricVertex, asymmetricVertex, compressedSymmetricVertex and
  compressedAsymmetricVertex. Therefore ONLY use the vertex methods that also
  exist on compressed vertices: getOutDegree(), getInDegree(),
  decodeOutNgh / decodeInNghBreakEarly / decodeOutNghSparse /
  decodeOutNghSparseSeq / countOutNgh / packOutNgh / copyOutNgh.
  *** DO NOT call getOutNeighbor(j) / getOutNeighbors() / getInNeighbor(j) in an
  app *** -- those do not exist on compressed vertices and the app must keep
  compiling once Ligra+ compressed vertices are implemented. If you need the
  neighbour list, materialize it with copyOutNgh (see apps/Triangle.C for the
  exact idiom) or use countOutNgh with a predicate.
* Read /workspace/apps/BFS.C, /workspace/apps/PageRank.C and
  /workspace/apps/Triangle.C first -- match their style, comment density and
  the 23-line MIT licence header they carry.
* /workspace/tutorial/*.C contains SKELETONS with "//FILL IN" markers showing
  the intended structure of some apps. Use them as structural hints only.

Inputs: ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (symmetric, unweighted, n=128 m=708,
run with -s) and ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 (symmetric, WEIGHTED, run with -s).

Always finish by actually building and running your app and confirming the
output is sane. Report exactly what you ran and what it printed.


You are an INDEPENDENT VERIFIER for /workspace/apps/Components-Shortcut.C, which another agent just wrote.

The spec it was given was:
Implement /workspace/apps/Components-Shortcut.C -- connected components by
label propagation WITH POINTER JUMPING (shortcutting).
* Same CC_F update/updateAtomic/cond as the plain Components algorithm
  (writeMin of IDs, guarded by prevIDs).
* Additionally a CC_Shortcut functor used with vertexFilter/vertexMap that
  performs pointer jumping: IDs[i] = IDs[IDs[i]] repeatedly collapses the
  label forest so labels converge in fewer rounds. A vertex stays active only
  while its label keeps changing.
* Initial frontier = all n vertices. Loop until the frontier is empty.
* IMPORTANT correctness requirement: the final component labelling must induce
  EXACTLY the same partition of vertices as apps/Components.C. State in your
  report the number of components you observed so it can be cross-checked.
* Report "Components-Shortcut rounds: <N>" and "Components: <N>" (number of
  distinct components, same counting rule as Components.C).
* Run: ./Components-Shortcut -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100

Its report was:
File is clean and final. Here is the report.

**File written:** `/workspace/apps/Components-Shortcut.C` (only file touched; nothing under `/workspace/ligra/` or `apps/Makefile` modified — the `M apps/Makefile`, `M ligra/ligra.h`, `?? ligra/byte*.h` entries in git status pre-date me / belong to other agents)

**Commands run**
```
cd /workspace/apps && make Components-Shortcut
   -> g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o Components-Shortcut Components-Shortcut.C     (clean, no warnings in my file)
cd /workspace/apps && ./Components-Shortcut -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
cd /workspace/apps && ./Components-Shortcut -s ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100              (default -rounds 3, idempotence)
g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -DLONG -DEDGELONG -o /tmp/cs_long Components-Shortcut.C ; /tmp/cs_long -s -rounds 1 ...
```

**Full stdout of the required run**
```
Components-Shortcut rounds: 4
Components: 4
Components-Shortcut rounds: 4
Components: 4
Running time : 1.5e-05
```
(two blocks = parallel_main's untimed warm-up call + 1 timed round; `-rounds 3` gives 4 identical blocks, so Compute is idempotent. The `-DLONG -DEDGELONG` build prints the same 4/4.)

**Cross-check numbers for Components.C**
- `Components: 4` on `rMatGraph_J_5_100` (n=128, m=708). Component sizes 125, 1, 1, 1; component minima are 0, 1, 5, 40 (vertices 1, 5, 40 are isolated).
- Verified against an independent Python union-find over the same adjacency file, via a temporary `-dumpids` debug print (since removed, binary rebuilt without it): the final `IDs[]` array is **element-wise identical to the component minima**, not merely partition-equivalent. Both counting rules agree: 4 distinct labels, and 4 vertices with `IDs[i] == i`.
- `Components-Shortcut rounds: 4` vs. plain label propagation, which needs one more round on this graph (the shortcut collapses the last chain a round earlier).

**Design notes / concerns**
- `CC_F` is the upstream form: `update` does the guarded plain write, `updateAtomic` is `writeMin(&IDs[d],IDs[s]) && origID == prevIDs[d]`, `cond` is `cond_true`. `prevIDs` (synced by `CC_Vertex_F` at the top of each round) makes each vertex enter the output frontier exactly once per round.
- `CC_Shortcut` is used with `vertexFilter(output, ...)`: it walks `IDs[i] -> IDs[IDs[i]] -> ...` to the root of the label tree and writes the result with `writeMin` (not a plain store), then returns `prevIDs[i] != IDs[i]` so a vertex stays active only while its label keeps changing. Two invariants make this safe: `IDs[x] <= x` always holds (so the chain strictly decreases and cannot cycle), and every label on the chain is a vertex of `i`'s own component (so shortcutting never crosses components).
- Deliberate subtlety: the shortcut writes **only** `IDs[i]`, never intermediate nodes on the path. Compressing intermediates would change the label of vertices that are not in the next frontier, and that change would never reach their neighbours — that variant is a real correctness bug, which is why the walk is read-only except for `i`.
- `output.toDense()` is called before `vertexFilter` because `vertexFilter` takes its `vertexSubset` **by value** and calls `toDense()` on the copy; materializing it first means `output.del()` actually frees that array instead of leaking it each round.
- Uses only `getOutDegree`/`decode*` paths through `edgeMap`, no `getOutNeighbor(s)`; the file compiles for `symmetricVertex`, `asymmetricVertex`, `compressedSymmetricVertex` and `compressedAsymmetricVertex` (confirmed by the instantiation contexts in the `-Wall` output).
- The weighted input `rMatGraph_WJ_5_100` is not applicable here — this is an unweighted app (`update(s,d)` signature); it would need a `-DWEIGHTED` build with 3-argument updates.

Your job: try to REFUTE that this app is correct and complete.
1. Read the file. Check it really implements the named algorithm (not a stub or a
   trivially-wrong shortcut), that it is `template <class vertex>`, and that it
   does NOT call getOutNeighbor/getOutNeighbors/getInNeighbor/getInNeighbors
   (those break on compressed vertices later).
2. Rebuild from scratch: cd /workspace/apps && rm -f Components-Shortcut && make Components-Shortcut
   -- it must compile with no errors. Warnings are acceptable.
3. Run it and check the printed numbers are actually right. Where feasible,
   compute the ground truth INDEPENDENTLY with a small python script over
   /workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (or rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 for the weighted
   app) and compare. Do not trust the implementation's own claims.
4. Confirm it does not modify anything under /workspace/ligra/, the Makefile,
   or another app (check: cd /workspace && git status --short).

If you find a real defect, FIX IT in Components-Shortcut.C (that file only), rebuild,
rerun, and re-verify. Then report.

Return: VERDICT (PASS or FIXED or BROKEN), the ground-truth values you computed
independently, the values the app printed, and anything still wrong.

cat > /tmp/gt.py <<'EOF'
import sys
p='/workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100'
tok=open(p).read().split()
assert tok[0]=='AdjacencyGraph'
n=int(tok[1]); m=int(tok[2])
off=[int(x) for x in tok[3:3+n]]
edges=[int(x) for x in tok[3+n:3+n+m]]
assert len(edges)==m, (len(edges),m)
adj=[[] for _ in range(n)]
for u in range(n):
    s=off[u]; e=off[u+1] if u+1<n else m
    adj[u]=edges[s:e]
# undirected union-find over the edge list (symmetric graph)
par=list(range(n))
def find(x):
    while par[x]!=x:
        par[x]=par[par[x]]; x=par[x]
    return x
def uni(a,b):
    ra,rb=find(a),find(b)
    if ra!=rb: par[max(ra,rb)]=min(ra,rb)
for u in range(n):
    for v in adj[u]:
        uni(u,v)
lab=[find(u) for u in range(n)]
# component min = root by construction (we always attach larger->smaller)
comps={}
for u in range(n):
    comps.setdefault(lab[u],[]).append(u)
mins=sorted(comps.keys())
print("n=%d m=%d"%(n,m))
print("num_components=%d"%len(comps))
print("component minima=",mins)
print("sizes=",[len(comps[k]) for k in mins])
# check symmetry of the adjacency
es=set()
for u in range(n):
    for v in adj[u]: es.add((u,v))
asym=[(u,v) for (u,v) in es if (v,u) not in es]
print("non-symmetric edge count=",len(asym))
selfloops=sum(1 for (u,v) in es if u==v)
print("self loops=",selfloops, "distinct directed edges=",len(es))
# also simulate the plain label-propagation round count and the shortcut round count
def sim(shortcut):
    IDs=list(range(n)); prev=list(range(n))
    frontier=set(range(n)); rounds=0
    while frontier:
        rounds+=1
        for i in frontier: prev[i]=IDs[i]
        out=set()
        for s in sorted(frontier):
            for d in adj[s]:
                o=IDs[d]
                if IDs[s]<o:
                    IDs[d]=IDs[s]
                    if o==prev[d]: out.add(d)
        if shortcut:
            nxt=set()
            for i in sorted(out):
                l=IDs[i]
                while l!=IDs[l]: l=IDs[l]
                if l<IDs[i]: IDs[i]=l
                if prev[i]!=IDs[i]: nxt.add(i)
            out=nxt
        frontier=out
    return rounds,IDs
r1,ids1=sim(False)
r2,ids2=sim(True)
print("sim plain rounds=%d  sim shortcut rounds=%d"%(r1,r2))
print("plain IDs == ground truth minima:", ids1==lab)
print("shortcut IDs == ground truth minima:", ids2==lab)
print("distinct labels plain=%d shortcut=%d"%(len(set(ids1)),len(set(ids2))))
EOF
